title: Consistent session rehydration and priority load shedding for active-active API gateways
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an active-active traffic shifting mechanism for the hosted API edge that preserves streaming session continuity (token/kv-cache preservation) while enabling priority-based load shedding and circuit breaking during regional saturation. This ticket covers design, an initial implementation of session rehydration, endpoint-level traffic priority tagging, rate-aware shedding rules, and a phased rollout with telemetry-driven guardrails.

Why now: Recent incidents show that blunt cross-region drains cause stream resets and user-visible truncation for long-running streaming conversations. We must provide a predictable, SLO-aligned failover that balances latency targets with unit-cost and availability SLOs for paying customers while avoiding cascading overload during repatriation windows.
rationale: We cannot treat streaming sessions the same as short stateless calls during failover. Preserving KV cache and message order is critical for user-facing chat experiences. Priority load shedding (per-customer or per-route) reduces tail risk and preserves high-value traffic when capacity is constrained. Circuit breakers must be regional and token-aware to avoid amplifying backpressure across replicas.
design_decisions: Session identity: use immutable session-id header (x-rw-session) propagated from edge through gateway to runtime; when absent gateway assigns a lightweight session token and returns it in initial response

Rehydration model: persist minimal rehydration artifacts (last 2k tokens KV snapshot + stream offset metadata) in regional fast-store (Redis cluster) with tombstone TTLs to limit cross-region sync cost
Failover modes: (A) soft-redirect (best-effort rehydrate) vs (B) hard-cutover (drain & re-establish) — default to soft-redirect for streaming unless explicit SLA pin forces hard-cutover
Priority tagging: routes and tokens carry priority labels (system, enterprise, paid, free-trial) used by shedding rules and canary policies
Circuit breaker placement: two-tier breakers — gateway-level (per-region) and runtime-level (per-model-pool) with token-count and error-rate thresholds
Telemetry-first gating: enable rollout gates based on real-time SRE metrics (session-loss-rate < 0.1% and 95th-latency within SLO budget)
implementation_notes: Edge: add x-rw-session header generation and validation; expose /sessions API for snapshot fetch with 50ms p95 target
Gateway: implement priority queue per worker and admission control that accounts for token-length of in-flight streaming requests
Runtime: extend KV-cache API to support snapshot export/import for rehydration; snapshots are versioned and signed
Fast-store: provision regional Redis clusters with 99.99% SLA; soft-TTL for snapshots default 15 minutes, configurable per-customer
Circuit-breaker: implement leaky-bucket-based tripping to avoid synchronized global trips; include gradual backoff and token-preservation mode
Config: new policy objects in control plane for priority-shedding rules and route-level rehydrate hints (e.g., prefer-rehydrate: true)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Canary: internal-only canary (10% internal traffic) in us-west with session rehydrate off by default (observe snapshot latency and success rate)
Phase 1 - Beta customers: enable prioritized rehydration for selected enterprise customers in us-west and eu-west with observability dashboards and SRE runbook on-call
Phase 2 - Progressive regional enablement: enable soft-redirect rehydration for all traffic in a region with telemetry gates (session-loss < 0.1% and 95th-latency within 150% of baseline)
Phase 3 - Global: enable cross-region rehydrate with local tombstone sync and full circuit breakers; monitor for cascading load and enable global backstop to route >90% traffic to less-loaded regions
Rollback: immediate kill-switch in Console to disable rehydration and revert to current hard-cutover flow; automated rollback if session-loss exceeds threshold for 5 minutes
testing_plan: Unit tests for session header generation and snapshot roundtrip
Synthetic streaming load test (k6 + custom token generator) that simulates 10k concurrent streams with varying message sizes
Chaos test: simulate regional outage and measure session-preservation rate, model cold-start latency, and tail token loss
Failure-mode tests: exercise partial Redis failure, KV snapshot corruption, and gateway overload to validate circuit-breaker behavior
SLO validation: run production shadow traffic for 48h and assert sla-tracker shows no regression >0.05% TTF (timeout/failure)
acceptance_criteria: Session-preservation: >= 99.9% of active streaming sessions are rehydrated successfully in soft-redirect mode during normal failover tests
SLO compliance: no increase in 95th latency beyond 20% for priority traffic after rollout
Circuit breaker: regional breakers trip and recover without cascading failures in simulated overloads
Observability: dashboards created for session-loss, snapshot-latency, rehydrate-failures, and shedding-rate; alert thresholds agreed with SRE
Runbook: verified runbook and migration checklist locked and approved by SRE and PM
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: session_rehydrate_success_rate, session_snapshot_latency_ms_p95, priority_shed_rate, gateway_circuit_tripped_count
Dashboards: Region overview + per-customer priority view; model-pool impact deck
Alerts: P0 if session_rehydrate_success_rate < 99% for >5m across >1 region; P1 if priority_shed_rate > 5% sustained for 10m
Oncall actions: immediate rollback instruction and diagnostic checklist (collect snapshots, triage traces)
